subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Nanotech for Imaging
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on DNA Nanotech for Imaging.

hook.text: DNA-PAINT achieves super-resolution microscopy below 5 nm — using blinking DNA strands instead of blinking fluorophores.

buildup.text: Short imager strands transiently bind to docking sites — each binding event creates a blink that localizes the target.

discovery.text: Unlike photobleaching fluorophores, DNA strands never tire — they bind, unbind, and repeat indefinitely.

twist.text: Multiplexing is easy — change the imager sequence and image a different target on the same sample, sequentially.

climax.text: DNA-PAINT resolved the 3D organization of proteins in cell membranes — seeing molecular architecture others could not.

punchline.text: Blinking DNA strands outperform dyes — sharper images, no bleaching, infinite colors.

quiz.question: What advantage does DNA-PAINT have over traditional fluorophore-based super-resolution microscopy?
options: DNA-PAINT uses larger probes that are easier to see
DNA strands bind and unbind indefinitely without photobleaching, enabling unlimited imaging
DNA-PAINT requires no microscope at all
